EU261.title: What the airline owes you while you wait

items.label: Meals and refreshments
items.detail: In reasonable relation to the waiting time. Ask for vouchers at the desk; if none are offered, keep receipts.

items.label: Two phone calls, emails or messages
Hotel and transport to it
items.detail: When the new departure is the next day or later.

items.label: Refund or return flight instead of travelling
items.detail: When the delay is 5 hours or more and you decide not to travel.

items.label: Rerouting or refund if cancelled
items.detail: Choose a refund, rerouting at the earliest opportunity, or rerouting at a later date that suits you.

items.label: Ask for the reason in writing
items.detail: Note what staff tell you and keep boarding passes, receipts and screenshots of airline messages.

US_DOT.title: What to ask for on a US flight
US_DOT.citation: 14 CFR Part 260 and the DOT Airline Customer Service Dashboard

items.label: Meal voucher
items.detail: Most large US airlines commit to meal vouchers for controllable delays of 3 hours or more. Check the DOT Airline Customer Service Dashboard for your airline.

items.label: Hotel for an overnight wait
items.detail: Many airlines commit to this when the delay or cancellation was within their control.

items.label: Cash refund if you don't travel
items.detail: If the flight is cancelled or arrives 3+ hours late (6+ international) and you decline the alternative, you are owed a refund, not a voucher.

items.label: Ask for the reason in writing
items.detail: Airlines' commitments usually depend on whether the cause was within their control.
